item.title: City ready to own bank property
item.description: A run-down building that was a bank along DeBary’s main street is about to change hands. Under an agreement ratified by the City Council, DeBary will take possession of the old Bank of America property at 150 S. Charles Richard Beall Blvd. and thus end a long-running code-enforcement case. “We anticipate closing in 30 days,” City Manager Carmen Rosamonda told […] The post City ready to own bank property first appeared on The West Volusia Beacon.

item.title: Museum Notes: The Florida Highwaymen
item.description: The Florida Highwaymen are one of the most inspiring and uniquely Floridian stories in American art. Composed of 26 Black artists who began painting in the 1950s segregated Jim Crow Florida, these painters sought to make a living in a time where most Black men and women were relegated to underpaid field work or difficult labor jobs. item.title: Sheriff Chitwood rescinds endorsement of Rep. Fine over controversial remarks
item.description: Volusia County Sheriff Mike Chitwood announced Thursday in a public Facebook post that he is withdrawing his support for U.S. Rep. Randy Fine, citing concerns about the congressman’s recent rhetoric toward Muslims. “Rep. Fine’s statements that have come to my attention recently just don’t align with my responsibility to stand up and protect the entire community,” Chitwood wrote. item.title: Roadblock on U.S. 92 after fatal crash
item.description: A fatal car crash around 10 a.m. Feb. 19 shut down traffic on U.S. Highway 92 between LPGA Boulevard and Tomoka Farms Road, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. A 54-year-old Deltona woman traveling eastbound lost control and overturned her vehicle. This story will be updated when more information is available. The post Roadblock on U.S. 92 after fatal crash first appeared on The West Volusia Beacon.

item.title: Truck crash forces closure of Heritage Inn; residents relocated
item.description: A truck crash Tuesday, Feb. 17, left the Heritage Inn in Orange City unsafe for occupancy, displacing guests and prompting a coordinated response from city officials and relief agencies. According to an official statement from the City of Orange City, the crash caused significant damage to the hotel’s power source, structural components, water service and fire suppression system. item.title: Lake Helen police chief Robert Mullins to retire
item.description: Police Chief Robert B. Mullins will retire effective April 30, 2026, concluding a 28-year career with the Lake Helen Police Department.
